title: ML-KEM Key Exchange
description: Establishes shared secrets with the Module Learning-With-Errors problem, standardized by NIST as ML-KEM (FIPS 203). It replaces Diffie-Hellman and ECDH in protocols like TLS, keeping key exchange safe against quantum attackers.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: ML-DSA Signatures
description: Signs with the Module Short-Integer-Solution problem, standardized as ML-DSA (FIPS 204), the quantum-safe replacement for RSA and ECDSA signatures. Certificates, firmware, and software updates move to ML-DSA to stay verifiable in a post-quantum world.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: The LWE Problem
description: Learning With Errors asks an attacker to solve noisy linear equations - easy without noise, believed hard with it, even for quantum computers. LWE's hardness underpins the security proofs of lattice cryptography.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Module Lattices
description: Works over module lattices - structured generalizations balancing efficiency and security - which is what makes ML-KEM and ML-DSA practical. The module structure enables fast NTT-based arithmetic without the risks of overly structured rings.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Parameter Sets
description: Chooses among standardized parameter sets trading security level against key and signature size. Picking the right set - not too weak, not wastefully large - is the central practical decision in deploying post-quantum crypto.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Hybrid Classical plus PQC
description: Combines classical and post-quantum algorithms so security holds if either one breaks, the prudent posture during the transition. Hybrids are the recommended deployment pattern while PQC matures.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Key Sizes
description: Plans for post-quantum key sizes - kilobytes, not bytes - across protocols, storage, and bandwidth budgets. Size planning prevents the surprise of PQC keys not fitting in constrained fields designed for ECC.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Side-Channel Resistance
description: Implements lattice operations in constant time with masked secrets, since PQC's larger operations offer more side-channel surface. Resistance is tested with leakage detection, not assumed from clean code.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Known-Answer Tests
description: Validates implementations against official KAT vectors, catching the subtle bugs that make two 'correct' implementations disagree. KATs are the first gate every PQC implementation must pass.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Migration Guides
description: Lays out the inventory-discover-prioritize-migrate path: find all crypto use, rank by exposure and lifetime, migrate in order. Guides turn a decade-long migration into a managed program.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Certificate Formats
description: Encodes PQC keys and hybrid chains in X.509 certificates so existing PKI tooling carries them. Format work ensures the world's certificate infrastructure can actually transport post-quantum keys.

title: TLS Integration
description: Negotiates PQC key exchange in TLS 1.3 handshakes, the highest-impact deployment target since TLS secures the web. Integration work focuses on handshake size and middlebox tolerance.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Firmware Signing
description: Signs firmware with ML-DSA so devices stay authentically updatable after quantum computers arrive. Firmware is the longest-lived signed artifact, making it the most urgent PQC signature migration.

title: Performance Benchmarks
description: Measures PQC operation speeds across platforms so protocol designers know the real costs - keygen, encaps, decaps times on hardware from servers to microcontrollers. Benchmarks ground deployment decisions in data.

title: Security Levels
